fields.ic_name: ARM Serial Wire Debug (SWD) — ADIv5 (ARM IHI 0031C)
fields.security_requirements_present: partial — ADIv5 itself does not standardize debug-authentication or debug-disable, but ARM has layered a debug-authentication interface (DBGEN / NIDEN / SPIDEN / SPNIDEN) on top of the DAP that all Cortex-A and most Cortex-M parts implement. Per-vendor SoCs add OTP fuse-based debug-disable mechanisms.
fields.notes: ARM IHI 0031C describes the wire-level + register-level debug-access protocol; it does not require confidentiality, integrity, or authentication features at the protocol layer. Any debug probe wired to SWCLK + SWDIO of an un-protected SoC has full access to the CPU + system bus including flash contents. Real-world Arm-based MCUs always layer some form of debug protection on top — usually via OTP fuses programmed at production test. The most common mechanisms are listed below.
industrial_security_extensions_layered_o: ARM CoreSight DBGEN/NIDEN/SPIDEN/SPNIDEN — 4-bit external authentication signal that gates which debug paths are enabled: DBGEN = invasive (halt + breakpoint) debug; NIDEN = non-invasive (trace + PC sample) debug; SPIDEN = invasive debug in Secure state; SPNIDEN = non-invasive debug in Secure state. Typically driven by an on-chip Secure ROM after authentication challenge.
ARMv8-M Security Extension — TrustZone for Cortex-M; debug access to Secure address space is gated by SPIDEN; non-secure debug is gated by DBGEN.

ST Read-Out Protection (RDP) — STMicroelectronics RDP Level 0 = full debug; Level 1 = limited debug + flash erase on debug unlock; Level 2 = permanent debug disable + flash content protected (one-way fuse).
Nordic UICR.APPROTECT — Nordic SoCs: SET = SWD reaches only the bootloader region; UNSET = SWD reaches anything; once SET to a non-default value, full re-enable requires mass-erase.
NXP DCFG / KW3 + Secure Boot — debug-disable fuses programmable at production; can be partial (debug only of non-secure code) or full.
ESP32 / ESP32-S3 efuse JTAG_DISABLE — full SWD/JTAG disable via one-way fuse.
Renesas Synergy Security MPU — debug disable + flash content + flash-write protect.
Silicon Labs Secure Vault — TrustZone + AES-encrypted debug authentication.
Microchip SAMD / SAMC ROM-protected debug — partial debug-disable via NVMCTRL fuse.
TI MSP432 / SimpleLink debug disable via JTAGLOCK + Customer Configuration Area (CCFG).
Atmel/Microchip CRYPTOAUTHLIB-based debug authentication — host probe must present a signed challenge to the on-chip secure element.
threat_model_for_open_swd: An attacker with physical board access can connect an SWD probe and read out flash contents via MEM-AP DRW transactions targeting flash mirror addresses.
Vendor-specific user-defined MEM-AP registers may expose secure-boot keys, OTP fuse contents, internal SRAM (compromising live secrets, encryption keys, RAM-resident firmware).
Glitch-injection attacks during the SWD power-up handshake can bypass debug-disable fuses on some vulnerable SoCs.
Side-channel attacks on the debug-authentication interface (DBGEN gating logic) can recover authentication secrets.
If the SWD pads are not removed or destroyed in production, an adversary can solder probes onto fine-pitch test pads and gain full debug access.
common_production_mitigations: Burn a debug-disable fuse at post-production test (RDP Level 2 / APPROTECT SET / JTAG_DISABLE blown).
Implement debug authentication via DBGEN/NIDEN/SPIDEN/SPNIDEN gating; require cryptographic challenge before enabling invasive debug.
Use TrustZone-M (Cortex-M33/M55) to isolate Secure code; Secure debug requires SPIDEN authentication.
Remove the SWD header from production boards (or use a non-standard footprint like TC2050 that requires specialized fixtures).
Disable the SWO trace pin in production to remove a side-channel for live tracing.
Implement read-out-only firmware that disables the SWD MEM-AP at first boot via a vendor-specific debug-config register write.
Use a Secure Boot ROM that mass-erases flash on detection of an unauthorized debug session attempt.
Physical countermeasures: tamper-detection mesh, anti-tamper trace destruction, package-level debug-pad obfuscation.
tooling_security_considerations: Open-source debug probes (CMSIS-DAP, Black Magic Probe) are easier to audit for malicious modifications.
Commercial probes (J-Link, ST-Link) include locked firmware that vendors update for security disclosures.
OpenOCD / pyOCD / probe-rs are open-source host-side libraries; their debug authentication support is vendor-dependent.
Always validate VDD-IO before connecting — wrong voltage can damage the target and may also bypass voltage-glitch debug protections.
